clinician.trajectory_summary: A 74-year-old male initially presented in 2005 with a one-year history of pruritic, cutaneous lesions on his left lower extremity, described as an erythematous plaque and cord-like nodular lesions. He was subsequently lost to follow-up. The patient returned to care in 2017, presenting with ulcers, perilesional induration, erythema, desquamation, and cord-like, firm, brown nodules on the left leg and thigh (E002). Histopathological examination of tissue obtained after 2017 revealed hyperkeratosis, epidermal acanthosis, a diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, giant cells, hemosiderin-laden histiocytes, and increased vascularity in the papillary dermis (E003). Further examination with Grocott's methenamine silver stain showed numerous round yeasts with thick double walls, occurring singly or in chains connected by tubular projections (E004), which are characteristic findings for Lobomycosis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented in 2017 with ulcers, perilesional induration, erythema, desquamation, and cord-like, firm, brown nodules on the left leg and thigh, consistent with chronic cutaneous infection.

Histopathological examination after 2017 showed hyperkeratosis, epidermal acanthosis, a diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, giant cells, hemosiderin-laden histiocytes, and increased vascularity in the papillary dermis.

Grocott's methenamine silver stain after 2017 revealed numerous round yeasts with thick double walls, occurring singly or in chains connected by tubular projections, which are pathognomonic for Lobomycosis.
